content.text:
I reviewed the full package — brief, disclosure, conversation (isolating the affirmative USER passages), all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs — and built a complete source ledger.

Key traces I confirmed:

- **Claims 1–20:** every limitation (rigid base with first/second sides, motor on the first side, air-extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, rigid low-friction perimeter loop terminating in an end/bearing face, clearance along at least part of the member admitting ambient air, extraction rate maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber pressure, all-rigid vibration path with no elastomer/foam/resilient mount, slidability under a maintained differential, plastic/metal/PTFE/combination materials, vacuum pump, continuous running, handle for guiding, rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled control, and the method steps) traces to explicit disclosure sentences. Claim 10's stirring elements trace to the one affirmative USER message ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"), which also supports the Field's "autonomously moving" and the FIG. 6 embodiment.
- **Numerals 10–48:** each has exactly one meaning across description, claims, briefs and ledger; the 28/30/32 gaps are unused, not conflicting.
- **Section designations:** 2-2 and 4-4 appear identically in the FIG. 3 source-view brief, the FIG. 2/FIG. 4 resulting-view briefs, and the Brief Description.
- **Figure briefs:** every substantive geometry statement is either disclosed (loop at the perimeter, band standing on the tile, layer stack tile/bonding material/substrate, clearance under the bearing face, mechanism on the first side) or expressly confined to the brief as a convention (rectangular plan, frame width, leg depth, block placement, flat lower end of the column, stirring-element number and position). No convention statement leaks into the application text as "by way of example" or an optional shape embodiment.
- **Timeline check:** the "five sheets" instructions all predate the stirring-element disclosure, so the six-figure set is not inconsistent with any later USER instruction.

The only item I weighed at length was the FIG. 2 schematic gap through the slab. I concluded it is supported: the inventor affirmatively discloses that the mechanism "is in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side of the base," the route through the base is forced by that first-side/second-side arrangement, the relationship is claimed (so it must be shown), and the brief verbalizes no taper, angle, depth, end position or contact topology — its width, position and form are disclaimed within the brief only.

No drafting notes, placeholders, questions, instructions to a person, or unresolved alternatives remain in any section body.

Every limitation of all twenty claims (device claims 1-10, system claims 11-15, method claims 16-20) was traced to exact disclosure sentences: rigid base with first and second sides, motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, rigid low-friction perimeter loop/skirt terminating in an end bearing face, the non-sealing clearance admitting ambient air beneath the perimeter, the extraction rate maintaining the chamber below atmospheric pressure, the all-rigid vibration path free of elastomeric, foam or resilient members, sliding under a continuously maintained differential, plastic/metal/PTFE/combination materials, vacuum pump, guiding handles, and the rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled position-versus-hold control. Claim 10 and the FIG. 6 embodiment trace to the single affirmative USER passage adding small stirring elements and vibration-driven constant forward motion, which also supports "autonomously moving" in the Field; the numerous resume/repair/audit instructions were treated as operational and not as disclosure. All seventeen numbered parts (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) carry one meaning each across the description, claims, numeral table and all six figure briefs, with no numeral defined in a brief that is absent from the ledger or the Brief Description. All six figure briefs and the corresponding Brief Description entries were compared part by part and match in cut bodies, omitted parts, schematic recitals and numeral sets; section designations 2-2 and 4-4 use the same repeated designation in the FIG. 3 source-view brief, in the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 resulting-view briefs, and in the drawing description. Every drawn structure is either affirmatively disclosed (loop at the perimeter of the second side, bearing face standing on the tile, clearance beneath the bearing face, covering element bedded in bonding material over a substrate, motor and extraction mechanism on the first side, pulling element connected to the device) or confined inside the figure brief as a stated depiction convention (rectangular plan form, frame width, leg and band depth, block order and spacing, flat lower end of the column, stirring-element number and drawn position); no convention statement leaks into the application text as "by way of example", "any closed outline", or a speculative optional embodiment. The FIG. 2 schematic gap between the housing interior and the chamber was examined under the functional-surface-geometry rule and found supported, because fluid communication between a first-side mechanism and a second-side chamber is affirmatively disclosed and claimed, the through-base route is forced by that disclosed arrangement, and the brief verbalizes no taper, angle, depth, end position, runout or contact topology, its width, position and form being disclaimed within the brief alone. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any section body, and the title, cross-reference and government-support statements follow the filing brief. The ledger closed with no untraced technical assertion and no verified internal inconsistency.
